# Compliance Vine — Engineering

> Public engineering pages for Compliance Vine (Joy of Wine Company Inc.), the compliance
> automation platform for direct-to-consumer wine shipping. The product source code is
> private; these pages are the public record of the engineering discipline behind it.
> Internal identifiers, credentials, customers, and infrastructure details are redacted by
> design.

The document most useful to a shopping agent or commerce platform is the pre-sale
verification contract: whether a specific seller may lawfully ship a specific basket to a
specific address, answered before payment.

Note on accuracy: `POST /api/v1/presale/verify` is a **draft contract and is not
deployed**. No base URL is published for it, and the OpenAPI document deliberately
declares no `servers` block. Do not infer or construct an endpoint.

## Agentic commerce

- [Before an AI recommends the bottle](https://joy-of-wine-company.github.io/engineering/agentic-commerce.md):
  Engineering memo. Why a shopping agent cannot infer whether a wine recommendation is
  lawful to fulfill, the two behaviours that invert when no human reviews the result, the
  five statuses, and the four invariants.
- [Pre-sale verification contract](https://joy-of-wine-company.github.io/engineering/docs/presale-verification.md):
  Request and response shapes, the full reason-code table, error handling, and guidance on
  what an agent may and may not tell a shopper for each status.
- [Verdicts and reason codes](https://joy-of-wine-company.github.io/engineering/docs/verdicts-and-reason-codes.md):
  Both vocabularies — checkout-time `PASS`/`BLOCK`/`QUARANTINE` and the pre-sale five —
  and the mapping between them. Explains why `seller_*` reason codes must never be
  generalised to a whole jurisdiction.
- [Authentication](https://joy-of-wine-company.github.io/engineering/docs/authentication.md):
  Credentials, why the request carries no account identifier, the opaque token format, and
  how each token degrades when absent or malformed.
- [Worked examples](https://joy-of-wine-company.github.io/engineering/examples/):
  Five request/response pairs — eligible, ineligible, age-required, review, timeout — each
  recording what an agent may and may not say.
- [OpenAPI 3.1 draft](https://joy-of-wine-company.github.io/engineering/openapi/cv-live-presale-v1.json):
  Machine-readable contract. Declares no `servers`, deliberately.

## Engineering memos

- [Distance to Five Nines](https://joy-of-wine-company.github.io/engineering/):
  The data-quality program — measuring compliance rule data the way SREs measure uptime,
  with the unedited climb log including every denominator corrected downward for honesty.
- [Platform architecture](https://joy-of-wine-company.github.io/engineering/platform.html):
  One intelligence engine behind every compliance decision, and what the rule data powers.
- [How we test a compliance engine](https://joy-of-wine-company.github.io/engineering/testing.html):
  External ground truth, adversarial bypass testing, parity fixtures, resilience, evidence.
- [Fail-safe by design](https://joy-of-wine-company.github.io/engineering/failsafe.html):
  How the system fails on purpose — legality fails closed into review, tax fails open to a
  floor that never over-collects. Essential background for why the pre-sale contract
  inverts the timeout behaviour.

## Optional

- [Case study (PDF)](https://joy-of-wine-company.github.io/engineering/compliance-savings-case-study.pdf):
  ~$160K combined first-year labor and software savings for one multi-state shipper.
- [Joy of Wine Company](https://joyofwine.co): The commercial site.
- [Canonical agentic-commerce page](https://joyofwine.co/developers/agentic-commerce):
  The same contract on the main site, with commercial and access information.
- [DTC wine compliance guide](https://joyofwine.co/compliance-guide): Public regulatory
  reference for all 50 states and the District of Columbia.
